subject: science
passage: In November 1974, at Hadar in the Afar region of Ethiopia, two researchers searching for fossils spotted a fragment of an arm bone on the slope of a gully. Over the following weeks, their team recovered several hundred pieces of bone representing about 40 percent of a single skeleton, later dated to roughly 3.2 million years ago. The researchers who celebrated the discovery at their camp that ______ the skeleton "Lucy," after the Beatles song "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds," which was playing repeatedly on a tape recorder.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the last sentence is "The researchers who celebrated the discovery at their camp that night," and its verb is "named." The "who" clause is essential: it tells which researchers the sentence means, so it is not set off with commas. With no opening comma after "researchers," no punctuation belongs before "named."
explanation.A: Correct. The essential "who" clause is not set off, so the long subject connects directly to its verb "named."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A long subject makes a comma tempting, but a single comma can't separate the subject from its verb "named," and the essential "who" clause needs no commas.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A dash can't separate the subject from its verb "named"; nothing here opens a pair of dashes.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon would separate the subject from its verb "named," and neither side would be an independent clause.
